name: oscar64-docs-mcp

tools.name: search
tools.description: Search across manual topics, tutorials, samples, and header files. Returns up to 10 ranked results. Examples: 'sprite collision', 'sid_init', 'raster interrupt'. Use result URIs with read_uri to get full content.

query.description: Query text, symbol, API name, or error phrase to search for. Examples: 'sprite', 'sid_init', '$d020 border'

type.description: Filter results by artifact type. Use 'headers' to find API functions, 'tutorials' for guides, 'samples' for code examples, or 'topics' for manual sections. Defaults to `all`.

system.description: Target system filter. Defaults to `c64`. Specify another system (nes, vic20, etc.) if needed.

tools.name: read_uri
tools.description: Read full text or binary content for docs:// and code:// URIs. Pass URIs from search results or list_indexes. Example URIs: 'docs://oscar64/manual#moving-image-blocks-sprites', 'code://oscar/include/c64/vic.h'. Anchors are slugified heading names (lowercase, hyphens, no special chars).

uri.description: A `docs://` or `code://` URI to read. Pass URIs from search results.

binary_mode.description: For binary files: return metadata only, or include base64 content. Size limit (256KB) applied automatically.

tools.name: list_indexes
tools.description: List all available topics, tutorials, samples, or headers with their URIs and anchors. Use this to discover valid URIs when you don't have a specific query. For topics, the anchor (e.g., #sprites) is shown in the name. Returns concrete docs:// or code:// URIs ready for read_uri.

type.description: Filter indexes by type. Defaults to `headers` (most common for API lookups). Use `all` to see everything, or filter to specific types for focused browsing.

system.description: Target system filter. Defaults to `c64`. Specify another system (nes, vic20, etc.) if needed.

instructions: Search Oscar64 compiler documentation, code examples, and API references. Typical workflow: (1) use `search` to find relevant content, (2) use `read_uri` to read full content from search results, (3) use `list_indexes` to discover available headers/tutorials/samples when browsing. Results are pre-ranked by relevance - start with high-confidence matches.
